sentences.text: Carnufex was among the largest crocodylomorphs of the Triassic period, yet it exhibits a mix of features found in both crocodylomorphs and their distant ancestors like the reptile Postosuchus.
The animal is highly autapomorphic, possessing many unique features that distinguish it from its close relatives.

Its dentition was specialized for predation, with premaxillary teeth that were slender, serrated, and recurved, while the maxillary teeth were serrated and knife-like with a significantly convex front edge and a slightly concave rear side.
The posterior process of the maxilla was circular in cross-section at the front but deepened and thinned towards the rear, and the antorbital fenestra was a very large and elongated triangular hole.
The outer surface of the jugal bone was covered with pits and ridges, and the cervical neural arch was a complex bone featuring nine laminae and twelve fossae.
The humerus was short with a constricted shaft.
Based on the holotype, Carnufex was estimated to be about 3 meters long and 1.5 meters tall, though it may have grown larger as the specimen was immature.
The genus Carnufex was first described in 2015 by Zanno et al. with the species name Carnufex carolinensis, which translates to "Carolina butcher".
Carnufex was the largest known carnivore in its ecosystem, but this might be due to sampling bias hiding larger predators like rauisuchids.
Carnufex is classified as a primitive crocodylomorph, belonging to a group of suchians more derived than Rauisuchidae.
Phylogenetic analysis suggests Carnufex is the most basal crocodylomorph, sharing this position with an unnamed genus.
Fossils of Carnufex date to the Carnian age of the Late Triassic, with a time range from 237 to 227.3 million years ago.
Carnufex was an extinct genus of crocodylomorph suchian that lived in North America during the Late Triassic.
